title: DEVELOPING A GAME-BASED PLATFORM FOR STUDENTS TO LEARN PROGRAMMING
text_snippet: DEVELOPING A GAME-BASED PLATFORM FOR STUDENTS TO LEARN PROGRAMMING This research centers on the development and validation of a game-based platform for programming learning, aimed at enhancing student engagement and motivation in introductory programming courses. The platform integrates live coding features with game elements, including characters, points, badges, leaderboards, and interactive challenges. Employing a research and development approach through the waterfall model, the study encompassed stages of requirement analysis, system design, implementation, and testing. Testing phases included unit testing, system testing, and user testing to ensure technical functionality and user satisfaction. A total of 276 Informatics students from Universitas Wijaya Kusuma Surabaya participated, using the platform over a five week period. User satisfaction was assessed with the End User Computing Satisfaction (EUCS) instrument, evaluating key dimensions such as content, format, ease of use, timeliness, and accuracy. The findings indicated high levels of user satisfaction, with scores exceeding 4.00, signaling positive reception and readiness for broader application in programming learning. title: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF H5P-BASED MATERIAL FOR TECHONOLOGY AND LIVELIHOOD EDUCATION (TLE) SPECIALIZED COURSES GUIDED BY THE ISO 9126 SOFTWARE QUALITY FRAMEWORK
text_snippet: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF H5P-BASED MATERIAL FOR TECHONOLOGY AND LIVELIHOOD EDUCATION (TLE) SPECIALIZED COURSES GUIDED BY THE ISO 9126 SOFTWARE QUALITY FRAMEWORK This paper evaluates the quality of an H5P-based review material developed for Technology and Livelihood Education (TLE) specialization courses undertaken as part of licensure examination review program. Using the ISO 9126 software quality framework, 85 fourth-year college students and 22 faculty members assessed the material across dimensions of functionality, reliability, usability, efficiency, maintainability, and portability. Findings revealed that both students and teachers strongly agreed on the material’s functionality and usability, indicating its effectiveness in delivering core instructional tasks and user-friendly design. However, reliability consistently received the lowest ratings, suggesting concerns about system stability and error handling. The Friedman test revealed significant within-group differences across quality dimensions for both teachers (χ² = 12.90, p = .025) and students (χ² = 41.40, p < .001). Durbin–Conover post hoc tests identified multiple significant pairwise differences, particularly highlighting usability and reliability gaps. title: REGULATORY EFFECTS OF GENERATIVE AI ON SELF-REGULATED LEARNING AND AI LITERACY: A MIXED-METHODS STUDY
text_snippet: REGULATORY EFFECTS OF GENERATIVE AI ON SELF-REGULATED LEARNING AND AI LITERACY: A MIXED-METHODS STUDY This study aimed to explicitly examine cognitive patterns of prompt engineering, the role of pre-service teachers’ artificial intelligence literacy (AIL) and online self-regulated learning (SRL) abilities in their use of prompting skills to develop lesson plans. The study was designed as a convergent parallel exploratory mixed-methods study involving quantitative analysis of students’ data on achievement in lesson planning, SRL and AIL, and qualitative interpretative exploration of students’ prompt sets based on cognitive domain and argumentation levels. The quantitative data was collected from 63 sophomore college students in a Faculty of Education through a quasi-experimental study with pre and post achievement tests, an AIL scale and an online learning self-regulation scale. The participants attended the experimental procedure with AIPRO. ORG in a computer laboratory within two hours. Two raters analyzed a total of 1070 prompts on the basis of hierarchical level of taxonomy of cognitive domain, and prompt sets on the basis of argumentative characteristics in three levels. The thematic analysis of the prompts revealed that the prompts were categorized into seven different themes.

Descriptive statistics, reliability analyses, Pearson’s correlation, independent-samples t-test, and multiple regression analyses were employed. The findings indicate that although students report high levels of perceived usefulness and ease of use regarding artificial intelligence technologies, they also exhibit notably high levels of perceived threat and future anxiety. title: COMPARING ONLINE AND FACE-TO-FACE DOCTORAL THESIS DEFENSES: A MIXED METHODS SWOT ANALYSIS
text_snippet: COMPARING ONLINE AND FACE-TO-FACE DOCTORAL THESIS DEFENSES: A MIXED METHODS SWOT ANALYSIS Doctoral thesis defenses are pivotal milestones in providing essential academic feedback and signifying key transitions in doctoral education. Traditionally held face-to-face, these defenses moved swiftly online, raising questions about their effectiveness and sustainability. This study uses an exploratory sequential mixed-methods approach to compare online and face-to-face doctoral thesis defenses using a SWOT analysis framework. The qualitative phase involved collecting data from 10 experienced thesis advisors, followed by a quantitative survey of 49 doctoral students from 14 academic departments. The findings highlight the distinct advantages of online defenses, such as increased spatial and temporal flexibility and the ability to record sessions for later reviews. However, ongoing technical difficulties and insufficient technical support pose significant weaknesses and threats to online defense formats. In contrast, face-to-face defenses excel at promoting strong interpersonal communication and dialogue, with genuine academic interactions identified as significant opportunities. text_snippet: ASSESSING PRESERVICE SOCIAL STUDIES TEACHERS’ EXPERIENCES IN DESIGNING DIGITAL MATERIALS DURING THE DISTANCE EDUCATION PROCESS The aim of this study is to assess the experiences of pre-service social studies teachers in designing digital materials during the distance education process, based on various variables. This study employed an embedded mixed-methods design. The study group consisted of thirty pre-service social studies teachers enrolled in a third-year “Material Design in Social Studies Teaching” course at a university in the Southeastern Anatolia region of Turkiye. Data collection instruments included the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge Self-Assessment Scale (TPACK-SAS), Individual Innovativeness Scale (IS), Technology Integration Strategies Scale (TIS), a semi-structured interview form, and participant diaries. The quantitative data were analysed using parametric and non-parametric tests, while qualitative data underwent thematic analysis. Mixedmethod integration was achieved through joint displays to combine quantitative and qualitative findings. title: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CONCEPTIONS AND APPROACHES TO TEACHING IN ONLINE DISTANCE EDUCATION COURSES
text_snippet: RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN CONCEPTIONS AND APPROACHES TO TEACHING IN ONLINE DISTANCE EDUCATION COURSES This study aimed to examine the relationship between conceptions and approaches to teaching in two forms of online teaching in a university in Vietnam; asynchronous teaching through video-recording and synchronous online teaching through online communication platforms. Data were gathered through interviews with 14 lecturers who taught through both modes of online teaching. Data analysis employed grounded theory. For the asynchronous online teaching via video-recording, there was no relationship between conceptions and approaches, as all lecturers used teacher-centred approaches to teaching. For the synchronous teaching through online communication platforms, there was a reasonably logical relationship between conceptions and approaches. Deviations from a logical relationship were caused by technological constraints. The findings differ markedly from those for face-to-face teaching, where there is normally a consistent and logical relationship between conceptions and approaches. This study highlights how technological affordances and institutional design choices mediate the expression of pedagogical intent in online distance education courses.

The blend of both instructional strategies creates effective and interactive learning sources and improves the perceived academic performance of learners in online learning mode. title: INTERACTIVE VIDEOS IN ASYNCHRONOUS ONLINE LEARNING: A PRISMA-COMPLIANT SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
text_snippet: INTERACTIVE VIDEOS IN ASYNCHRONOUS ONLINE LEARNING: A PRISMA-COMPLIANT SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS The increasing demand for inclusive and flexible learning has led to the widespread use of asynchronous online learning. In these settings, multimedia resources, especially educational videos, play a key role by offering content that supports various learning styles. However, creating meaningful interaction between learners and content remains a challenge. Interactive videos, such as those with embedded questions or scenario-based choices, offer new ways to keep learners engaged, reflective, and in control of their learning. This study used a PRISMA-compliant systematic literature review and bibliometric analysis to examine how interactive videos support learner–content interaction in asynchronous settings. A total of 38 studies were reviewed to identify trends, key themes, and research networks. The analysis identified three main perspectives (student, teacher, and generic) and four thematic areas: course design, interaction design, student experience, and evaluation. title: A HYBRID MODEL BASED ON MACHINE LEARNING AND GENERATIVE AI FOR PREDICTING ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE FROM LEARNING TRACES
text_snippet: A HYBRID MODEL BASED ON MACHINE LEARNING AND GENERATIVE AI FOR PREDICTING ACADEMIC PERFORMANCE FROM LEARNING TRACES The analysis of students’ learning traces in digital environments enables a better understanding of the factors influencing their academic performance. This paper proposes a hybrid predictive model combining Machine Learning (ML), Deep Learning (DL), and Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) to predict students’ academic performance (GPA) by leveraging traces from six dimensions: demographic, cognitive, social, emotional, contextual, and normative. First, the Random Forest algorithm is used to select the most relevant features. Then, a combined model based on MLP, LSTM, and XGBoost is trained to optimize prediction accuracy. Generative AI (DeepSeek) is integrated to enrich contextual data and provide personalized recommendations. Model decisions are interpreted using SHAP, allowing for explainability of the predictions. The model is evaluated on a real dataset of 1,002,393 records, built from learning traces collected from student interactions with courses hosted on a Moodle platform. title: BEYOND TRADITIONAL LEARNING: A HEUTAGOGICAL APPROACH TO ONLINE LEARNING FOR DOCTORAL STUDENTS
text_snippet: BEYOND TRADITIONAL LEARNING: A HEUTAGOGICAL APPROACH TO ONLINE LEARNING FOR DOCTORAL STUDENTS Interest in online learning has grown over the past decades, with the heutagogical approach gaining traction, especially in doctoral programs requiring learner autonomy. This study aims to explore doctoral students’ lived experiences with the heutagogical approach in online learning, including their perceptions of its effectiveness and their interpretation of learning outcomes and quality assurance processes. Using a phenomenological design, data were collected from graduate students at Universitas Negeri Yogyakarta, Indonesia, through indepth interviews and classroom observations over one semester. Observations revealed three key phases: (1) design (students co-developed learning objectives and project scopes aligned with their dissertations); (2) development (students conducted self-directed research with weekly discussions and iterative feedback); and (3) implementation (peer evaluations and final project submission for formal review). Students perceived the approach as effective, recognizing its flexibility and autonomy, while also acknowledging challenges such as demands for self-regulation, technical constraints, and limited face-to-face interaction. title: DEVELOPING A FRAMEWORK FOR ETHICAL IMPLEMENTATION OF GENERATIVE AI IN EDUCATION
text_snippet: DEVELOPING A FRAMEWORK FOR ETHICAL IMPLEMENTATION OF GENERATIVE AI IN EDUCATION This research examines key ethical points related to using generative artificial intelligence (AI) in education. As AI technologies advance, their application in creating personalized learning materials and automating educational tasks raises significant ethical challenges, including data privacy, algorithmic bias, authorship, and the evolving role of educators. This research presents a comprehensive ethical framework designed to guide educational institutions in the responsible implementation of generative AI. Through a systematic analysis of existing global guidelines, academic literature, and the identification of key gaps, this study develops actionable strategies to mitigate potential risks and ensure equitable AI-driven learning experiences. The proposed framework emphasizes context-specific guidelines, practical implementation steps, and continuous stakeholder engagement. A detailed case study illustrates the framework’s application in a real-world educational scenario. title: LEARNING NEEDS OF PRISON INMATES AND PERSPECTIVES OF DISTANCE EDUCATION
text_snippet: LEARNING NEEDS OF PRISON INMATES AND PERSPECTIVES OF DISTANCE EDUCATION The right to education is fundamental and must be provided to all without restriction. Distance learning methodologies present key learning opportunities for those with limited access to conventional education, such as prison inmates, and come in response to the demand for new solutions in the field of educational activities. The ever-increasing need for new forms of education highlights distance learning in prison schools as a key pillar of the new learning process. Education in prisons as a way of reintegrating offenders is an essential means of changing behavior patterns as well as for acquiring knowledge and developing-improving skills, while aiming at the smooth professional integration of inmates. The present study presents a review of distance education in prisons, as well as qualitative research examining aspects related to distance education in a prison of central Greece, which includes observation as well as interviews with thirty-six inmates. title: SURVEILLANCE OR SUPPORT? A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SUPPORTED PROCTORED ONLINE EXAMS
text_snippet: SURVEILLANCE OR SUPPORT? A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SUPPORTED PROCTORED ONLINE EXAMS Proctored online exams have become widespread, especially after COVID-19, increasing exam security and efficiency. In recent years, artificial intelligence developments have increased these systems’ importance by expanding their use. Accordingly, this study aims to provide an in-depth understanding of the conceptual structure of artificial intelligence-supported proctored online examination (AI-SPOE) research. Systematic literature review and text mining were used as methods. Thirty-two studies in Scopus and Web of Science databases were analyzed according to the PRISMA technique. While all the studies were examined in the context of content analysis, abstracts and keywords of the relevant studies were analyzed by text mining. The current study found it effective in increasing academic integrity and exam security, but problems such as privacy violations, exam anxiety, and algorithmic biases were encountered. Although methods such as biometric verification and behaviour analysis successfully detect cheating, technical difficulties, and false positives negatively affect the user experience. title: SELF-DIRECTED BLENDED LEARNING MODEL ON EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE AND ACHIEVEMENT
text_snippet: SELF-DIRECTED BLENDED LEARNING MODEL ON EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE AND ACHIEVEMENT In the era of advancing globalization, developing emotional intelligence (EI) has become essential for adolescents to manage emotional stress, build social relationships, and adapt to changing environments. This study developed a Self-Directed Blended Learning (SDBL) model incorporating Intangible Cultural Heritage music to enhance students’ EI and academic achievement. The research was conducted in two phases: First, the SDBL model was designed and validated, consisting of five components (setting learning targets, planning, gathering information, online and offline learning activities, and post-lesson reflection). Five education experts evaluated the model using a 5-point Likert scale, yielding an average score of 4.84, confirming its pedagogical quality. Second, the teaching experiment was conducted at Taiyuan University of Science and Technology. A total of 112 non-music undergraduate students, who voluntarily enrolled in the Shanxi Intangible Cultural Heritage Music Appreciation course, participated in the study. title: EXAMINING ENGLISH MAJORS’ PERCEPTIONS OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TEACHING PRESENCE, SATISFACTION AND ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENTS IN SYNCHRONOUS ONLINE CLASSES
text_snippet: EXAMINING ENGLISH MAJORS’ PERCEPTIONS OF THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN TEACHING PRESENCE, SATISFACTION AND ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENTS IN SYNCHRONOUS ONLINE CLASSES Growing interest in online education has led to considerable research on factors influencing students’ learning outcomes, yet research on the relationship between teaching presence and student satisfaction and academic achievements in synchronous online English classes in developing countries is scanty. The current study aimed to address this gap by employing a quantitative design and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) for data analysis. A total of 182 surveyed respondents from a private Vietnamese university, enrolling in various general English levels in synchronous online modes for at least one semester, completed a closed-ended five-point Likert scale questionnaire survey over a two-month period. The findings indicate that teaching presence was significantly associated with both extrinsic and intrinsic motivation, as well as student satisfaction in synchronous online English classes, although it does not directly influence academic performance. Extrinsic motivation showed a significant positive relationship with academic achievement, whereas intrinsic motivation shows no significant effect. title: UNDERSTANDING THE VALUE OF MICROCREDENTIALS IN HIGHER EDUCATION IN PAKISTAN
text_snippet: UNDERSTANDING THE VALUE OF MICROCREDENTIALS IN HIGHER EDUCATION IN PAKISTAN Today the world is witnessing a rapid change in industrial needs. Traditional education has failed to meet the current industrial demands. Micro-credentials have emerged as an innovative solution to address the evolving demands of higher education and workforce development to ultimately address the requirements of the changing industry. This research paper investigates the role of micro-credentials in strengthening educational quality and employability by offering targeted, competency-based certifications that complement traditional degree programs. Through a comprehensive analysis using mixed methods with a convergent design, the study reveals that micro-credentials facilitate flexible learning pathways, promote skills development, and provide institutions with a mechanism to align curricula with industry requirements. The findings indicate that students value the opportunity to receive specialized skills rapidly, while employers appreciate the direct correlation between micro-credential achievements and workforce readiness. title: A MULTIDISCIPLINARY UMBRELLA REVIEW ON FLIPPED LEARNING OUTCOMES
text_snippet: A MULTIDISCIPLINARY UMBRELLA REVIEW ON FLIPPED LEARNING OUTCOMES This umbrella review synthesizes evidence from 41 qualitative, meta-analytic, and mixed-method reviews to reveal the effectiveness of FL on cognitive, affective, and interpersonal domains across STEM, Medical and Health Sciences (M&H), and Social Sciences (SS). The results reveal that while flipped learning (FL) demonstrates positive effects on academic achievement in mathematics, science, and English language teaching, evidence for other domanial outcomes across fields remains inconclusive due to several limitations such as study scope, methodology and regional restrictions. Specifically, evidence across fields on other cognitive outcomes including autonomy, conceptual understanding, and higher-order thinking skills has the potential for fostering autonomy, conceptual understanding, and higher-order thinking skills, but the current evidence base is insufficient to definitively confirm these claims. title: TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF DIGITAL CURRICULUM IMPLEMENTATION IN JORDAN
text_snippet: TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF DIGITAL CURRICULUM IMPLEMENTATION IN JORDAN This study explores the perceptions of implementing digital curricula in terms of Readiness (technical and pedagogical) and the obstacles to implementation from teachers’ perspective in the Directorate of Education of Al-Jami’ah District, Jordan. The study employs a descriptive survey and includes a random sample of 370 male and female teachers working in the Directorate of Education of Al-Jami’ah District, Amman. A questionnaire was developed, focusing on two domains: teachers’ Readiness (technical and pedagogical) and the challenges of implementing digital curriculum supports. The results indicate that the overall Readiness for implementing digital curricula, in terms of technical and pedagogical Readiness, and the degree of obstacles to implementation were rated as moderate. There were significant differences in Readiness based on gender and school type, favoring males and private schools. However, no significant differences were observed concerning teaching experience or academic qualifications. The study recommends that stakeholders in the Ministry of Education prioritize digital curricula and work towards effective implementation in the educational field.

It was designed with a three-step approach involving translation and cross-cultural adaptation, pre-testing, and field testing. Subsequently, in the pre-testing phase, the English and Turkish versions of the scale were administered to a sample of 43 university students, and paired sample t-tests with Pearson correlation analyses were conducted to ensure content equivalence and reliability. In the field testing phase, data were collected from two independent student samples. title: USING FLIPPED LEARNING TO REDUCE MATHEMATICS ANXIETY OF PRIMARY SCHOOL STUDENTS
text_snippet: USING FLIPPED LEARNING TO REDUCE MATHEMATICS ANXIETY OF PRIMARY SCHOOL STUDENTS This study aimed to investigate the effects of flipped learning on mathematics anxiety among primary school students. An embedded mixed-methods design was employed for this study. The participants in the 8-week intervention were 3rd-grade primary school students attending a public school in Turkiye. Data for the study was collected through the use of the mathematics anxiety scale, interview form, student diaries, and observation instrument. The collected data was analysed utilizing the Wilcoxon Signed Rank Test for quantitative analysis and inductive content analysis methods for qualitative analysis. The quantitative analysis indicated that the flipped learning significantly reduced mathematics anxiety among primary school students and enhanced student participation. The qualitative analysis produced four main themes: in-class learning activities, student participation, technology and internet usage, and learning resources. The findings revealed that the incorporation of in-class learning activities in the flipped learning facilitated a better comprehension of mathematical concepts among students and fostered positive attitudes toward mathematics lessons.

A systemic-structural approach was employed as a general scientific method which made it possible to identify problematic issues in ensuring access to the educational process during wartime, to analyze the development of Ukrainian education in the context of integrative educational processes, and to formulate proposals aimed at improving the modern national education model. title: FROM ENTHUSIASM TO INITIAL INTEGRATION: EDUCATORS’ PERCEPTIONS AND PROMPT-DESIGN SKILLS IN USING CHATGPT FOR TEACHING
text_snippet: FROM ENTHUSIASM TO INITIAL INTEGRATION: EDUCATORS’ PERCEPTIONS AND PROMPT-DESIGN SKILLS IN USING CHATGPT FOR TEACHING The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) tools like ChatGPT into education presents significant opportunities to foster interactive and student-centered learning. This study surveyed 61 educators during an online AI workshop to examine their baseline prompt-design skills, explore their perceptions of student use of ChatGPT, and identify associated challenges and strategic opportunities. Importantly, the six-element prompt design framework was deliberately shared only after data collection, ensuring that the study captured prompt-design abilities at a true baseline without prior intervention, which constitutes a novel contribution of this research. Findings reveal that although most educators expressed enthusiasm for ChatGPT’s potential, there was notable variability in their ability to design effective prompts. Specifically, over 77% of the initial prompts were vague and lacked essential elements such as context, role, or format, indicating a substantial gap in prompt-engineering competence. title: BEHIND-THE-SCREEN BONDS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF PARASOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS IN PREDICTING LIVE SESSION PARTICIPATION AND EWOM IN OPEN AND DISTANCE LEARNING
text_snippet: BEHIND-THE-SCREEN BONDS: THE MEDIATING ROLE OF PARASOCIAL RELATIONSHIPS IN PREDICTING LIVE SESSION PARTICIPATION AND EWOM IN OPEN AND DISTANCE LEARNING This study, conducted within Anadolu University’s Open Education System, examines the effects of learners’ attitudes, subjective norms, and perceived behavioral control, as conceptualized in the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), on their intention to participate in live sessions and their intention to engage in electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM). It also tests the direct effect of parasocial relationships with instructors on these intentions, as well as their mediating role between TPB variables and behavioral intentions. Using the quantitative research method with a correlational research design, data were collected via an online survey from 475 open and distance learners who had attended at least one live session during the 2023–2024 fall semester. Data were analyzed using SPSS 25 and SmartPLS 4.0. Findings show that positive attitudes toward live sessions, high perceived behavioral control, and strong parasocial relationships significantly and positively influence both participation and eWOM intentions. title: UNDERSTANDING ACTUAL E-LEARNING ADOPTION: A COMPREHENSIVE TAM-BASED INVESTIGATION OF PRE-SERVICE MATHEMATICS TEACHERS
text_snippet: UNDERSTANDING ACTUAL E-LEARNING ADOPTION: A COMPREHENSIVE TAM-BASED INVESTIGATION OF PRE-SERVICE MATHEMATICS TEACHERS This study investigates the determinants of e-learning adoption among pre-service mathematics teachers through an extended Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) framework. Using structural equation modeling with data collected from 508 pre-service mathematics teachers in Indonesia, we examined thirteen hypothesized relationships between system accessibility, enjoyment, perceived ease of use, perceived usefulness, attitude toward using, behavioral intention, and actual system usage. Results revealed that system accessibility (β = 0.535) and enjoyment (β = 0.319) significantly predicted perceived ease of use, explaining 58.9% of its variance. Perceived usefulness was primarily influenced by enjoyment (β = 0.468), perceived ease of use (β = 0.323), and system accessibility (β = 0.165). Attitude toward using was significantly affected by perceived usefulness (β = 0.489) and perceived ease of use (β = 0.265), while behavioral intention was predominantly determined by perceived usefulness (β = 0.469), attitude toward using (β = 0.277), and perceived ease of use (β = 0.106). title: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF FEEDBACK MECHANISMS IN DISTANCE EDUCATION: EXPLORING SOURCES, TYPES, AIMS, FORMS, AND OUTCOMES
text_snippet: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF FEEDBACK MECHANISMS IN DISTANCE EDUCATION: EXPLORING SOURCES, TYPES, AIMS, FORMS, AND OUTCOMES Feedback plays a critical role in learning; however, its structure and implementation in distance education differ significantly from traditional educational practices due to the unique nature of online environments. This necessitates a systematic investigation into feedback mechanisms in distance education. This systematic review aims to explore the literature on feedback in distance education, focusing on the types, purposes, and timing of feedback, as well as their implementation and impact on students. We conducted a systematic search of relevant databases on May 5, 2024, without applying a publication year restriction, thereby including all eligible studies published up to that date in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. After applying inclusion and exclusion criteria, we included 91 studies and subjected them to content analysis. Existing literature guided the categorization of feedback, examining three dimensions: feedback types, purposes, and timing. Automated systems emerged as the most common source of feedback. title: MICRO-CREDENTIALS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW FOR QUALITY ASPECTS
text_snippet: MICRO-CREDENTIALS IN HIGHER EDUCATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW FOR QUALITY ASPECTS Quality assurance and accreditation is regarded as a significant facilitator and a barrier at the same time in the integration of micro-credentials in higher education. Micro-credentials can be used to complement and enhance education, training, lifelong learning and employability ecosystems without changing the nature of higher education and vocational training systems. Therefore, it is important to establish quality assurance and accreditation criteria to build trust in micro-credentials, facilitate their understanding and recognition, ensure their validity and reliability, and support the sustainability of micro-credentials. This study aimed to systematically analyze the literature, related reports and documents published between 2020 and 2024 to explore how the quality assurance of micro-credentials can be established. A total of 26 articles and 40 reports were thematically analyzed, generating free codes grouped into 22 categories and four themes: (1) integration into the higher education ecosystem and recognition, (2) institutional responsibility and capacity for change, (3) external quality assurance, and (4) challenges related to quality assurance and accreditation. title: EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE IN OPEN, DISTANCE, ONLINE AND DIGITAL EDUCATION
text_snippet: EMOTIONAL INTELLIGENCE IN OPEN, DISTANCE, ONLINE AND DIGITAL EDUCATION This bibliometric mapping study intended to explore research trends, key contributors, pioneering studies, predominant reach areas and topics as well as possible gaps related to emotional intelligence in the fields of open, distance, online and digital education. A total of 117 publications were included into analysis indexed in WoS and SCOPUS databases. The results have revealed that research in the field of emotional intelligence in ODODE is dynamic and growing. However, to realize its full potential, it needs to grow not only quantitatively, but also in terms of conceptual depth, methodological rigor and practical integration. By responding to the opportunities and challenges highlighted in this report, the field can make an important contribution to more humane, effective and inclusive digital learning environments. This research addresses questions concerning emotional intelligence in open, distance, online, and digital education, including the evolution of research over time, key contributors, seminal studies, dominant research domains and emerging topics, as well as unexplored areas for future investigation.

text_snippet: TEACHING PRESENCE AND ACADEMIC ACHIEVEMENT: THE MEDIATING ROLES OF SOCIAL AND COGNITIVE PRESENCES The purpose of this study was to explore the relations between teaching presence, social presence, cognitive presence and academic achievement based on a model testing the mediating role of social and cognitive presence between teaching presence and achievement. The study group of the study was composed of 248 preservice teachers, chosen based on the convenience sampling method. The Community of Inquiry Survey was used to determine pre-service self-reported perceptions on teaching presence, social presence and cognitive presence while pre-service teachers’ grades in the Research Methods in Education course was accepted as the academic achievement scores. Analysis based on the serial multiple mediator model showed that teaching presence not only directly and positively predicted academic achievement, but it also had an indirect and positive impact on academic achievement through social presence and cognitive presence. Results suggest that enhancing teaching presence improve academic achievement while it also serves to improve social and cognitive presences. text_snippet: PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF TEACHERS VIA DISTANCE EDUCATION: THE CASE OF NON-THESIS MASTER’S PROGRAM IN INNOVATIVE EDUCATION IN PRIMARY SCHOOLS The main aim of this study is to examine the opinions of the teachers studying in the Innovative Education in Primary School Distance Education Non-Thesis Master’s Program and the reflection of the program on their professional lives. In line with this aim, sequential explanatory design from mixed research methods was used in the study. 147 teachers participated in the quantitative part of the study and 52 teachers participated in the qualitative part. The data were collected through a questionnaire and a structured interview form. Descriptive statistics were used to analyze quantitative data and thematic analysis was used to analyze qualitative data. The study revealed that the majority of participating teachers participated in this program to improve their professional competencies and increase their teaching effectiveness. Participants gave positive evaluations of the live lessons, learning management system, content and assessment methods. It was stated that the program contributed significantly to teachers’ personal and professional development. title: ARE GRADUATE LEARNERS TRULY SATISFIED WITH ONLINE COURSES? EVIDENCE FROM ANADOLU UNIVERSITY
text_snippet: ARE GRADUATE LEARNERS TRULY SATISFIED WITH ONLINE COURSES? EVIDENCE FROM ANADOLU UNIVERSITY Although Anadolu University is known for having one of the world’s most prestigious and largest-scale Open Education Faculties, it also offers distance learning-based non-thesis master’s programs within its graduate education framework. The aim of this study is to explore the satisfaction of learners enrolled in distance education non-thesis master’s degree programs at Anadolu University regarding online courses delivered over the internet. This research was carried out using a cross-sectional survey model. 488 learners voluntarily participated in the study. The data obtained to determine the satisfaction of the learners towards online courses were collected using the ‘Satisfaction Scale for E-Courses’. As a result of the study, it was found that learners’ satisfaction with online courses differed significantly according to age, occupational status and monthly income level variables. Learners in the older age group were more satisfied with online courses than those in the young and young middle age group. text_snippet: DIGITAL SKILLS AND TECHNOLOGY USE IN EDUCATIONAL RESEARCH FOR TEACHER TRAINING IN DISTANCE EDUCATION In the rapidly evolving field of distance education, it is essential to equip in-service teachers with the digital competencies necessary to effectively integrate Information and Communication Technology (ICT) into educational research. This study explores the critical digital skills required in the in-service teacher training program at Universitas Terbuka, Indonesia, involving 445 participants across three provinces. Utilising Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS), the research examines key factors such as ICT anxiety, digital flow, digital skills, digital ethics, and the quality of ICT resources. The results reveal significant relationships between the quality of ICT resources and digital flow and ICT integration, highlighting the importance of infrastructure in enhancing educational practices. Notably, ICT anxiety is identified as a significant barrier that affects teachers’ willingness to adopt and integrate technology into their teaching methods, pointing to the psychological challenges associated with technology acceptance. title: CHATGPT’S AND HUMANS’ WRITTEN CORRECTIVE FEEDBACK IN EFL/ESL WRITING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
text_snippet: CHATGPT’S AND HUMANS’ WRITTEN CORRECTIVE FEEDBACK IN EFL/ESL WRITING: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW Written corrective feedback (WCF) is critical in EFL/ESL writing classrooms. This study aims to review existing research studies on the quality of WCF generated by ChatGPT and humans and to examine how WCF generated by ChatGPT can support WCF that humans give to students’ written work in higher education EFL/ESL writing contexts. To meet these goals, the researcher examined 23 studies published in 18 peer-reviewed journals from 2023-2024. The analysis results highlighted potential strengths and weaknesses of WCF generated by ChatGPT and humans. WCF generated by ChatGPT could review various aspects of writing and provide extensive descriptive feedback, yet it sometimes might experience system fatigue that affects the WCF quality. ChatGPT could also provide inaccurate WCF, give WCF that lacked human nuances, and were greatly influenced by how prompts were presented to it. Meanwhile, humans could provide aspects of WCF not accounted for ChatGPT, but their WCF might involve subjective judgment and be unclear. text_snippet: ENHANCING COLLABORATION AND DIGITAL LITERACY THROUGH ONLINE READING-CONCEPT MAPPING-RECIPROCAL TEACHING Teamwork and collaboration are essential for students as they can help them learn how to work effectively with others, preparing them for future academic and professional success. Collaboration skills are helpful in both traditional and digital face-to-face learning environments. Successful implementation of online learning also requires a strong foundation in digital literacy. This study aims to investigate the online Reading-Concept Mapping-Reciprocal Teaching (REMAP-RT) learning model to improve collaboration and digital literacy in higher education. We used a nonequivalent pretest-posttest control group design involving 89 students from three Biology Education study program classes at a state Islamic university in East Java province of Indonesia. Each class was studied using one of three methods: a) REMAP-RT, b) RT, and c) PD. A questionnaire was used to assess students' collaboration and digital literacy skills. Analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) was used to compare differences in collaboration and digital literacy among the three treatment groups based on questionnaire responses. title: CHANGING ASPECTS OF THE MANAGEMENT OF DISTANCE EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS DURING AI ERA: A CASE STUDY
text_snippet: CHANGING ASPECTS OF THE MANAGEMENT OF DISTANCE EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS DURING AI ERA: A CASE STUDY This study aimed to investigate how the era of artificial intelligence is transforming the management of distance education institutions, based on the perspectives of faculty members with expertise in distance education and administrative roles. Conducted as a qualitative case study, the research was carried out at a public open education faculty in Turkiye and involved twelve faculty members (five full professors, six associate professors, and one assistant professor), all experts in distance education. The data were collected through semi-structured interviews and analyzed through thematic analysis. The results of the study point out that artificial intelligence is driving substantial changes in decision-making, leadership practices, technology integration, and the management of teaching and learning processes. These changes reflect both opportunities and challenges, especially concerning institutional readiness, ethical leadership, and equitable access. Building on these findings, the study highlights the critical need for human-centric strategies, organizational capacity, and ethical governance to promote the sustainable adoption of AI technologies in distance education.

title: ENHANCING LECTURER PERFORMANCE: THE ROLE OF AGILITY IN TECHNO-ADAPTABILITY FOR DISTANCE EDUCATION
text_snippet: ENHANCING LECTURER PERFORMANCE: THE ROLE OF AGILITY IN TECHNO-ADAPTABILITY FOR DISTANCE EDUCATION The rapid integration of technology into distance education has resulted in an incomplete understanding concerning techno-adaptability and lecturer performance. Despite the topical nature of technology adoption, the role of agility or a multidimensional capability concerning cognitive, operational, and strategic responsiveness remains underexplored in the literature. This study investigates the moderating effect of agility on the relationship between techno-adaptability and lecturer performance in distance education. In this paper, the authors have used a quantitative explanatory design in which the data were gathered from 109 permanent lecturers through online questionnaires from the Mahardhika School of Economics, Surabaya City, Indonesia. The saturated sampling technique was used for the research study. The data were then analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The findings indicate that techno-adaptability significantly influences lecturers’ performance, while agility enhances this relationship. title: EVALUATION OF OPEN AND DISTANCE LEARNER PROFILE IN THE CONTEXT OF LEARNING STRATEGIES: AN ANALYSIS OF THE LATENT PROFILE IN TERMS OF DEEP AND SURFACE LEARNERS
text_snippet: EVALUATION OF OPEN AND DISTANCE LEARNER PROFILE IN THE CONTEXT OF LEARNING STRATEGIES: AN ANALYSIS OF THE LATENT PROFILE IN TERMS OF DEEP AND SURFACE LEARNERS The rapid evolution of digital technologies has significantly transformed educational methodologies, particularly in open and distance learning environments. Employing a quantitative, cross-sectional design, the study applies Latent Profile Analysis (LPA) to data collected from 1,045 students enrolled in the open education faculty at Anadolu University, Turkiye. This study investigates the latent profiles of open and distance learners in terms of their learning strategies, focusing on deep and surface learning approaches, and their perceptions of technology acceptance and barriers. Utilizing Latent Profile Analysis (LPA), the research identifies three distinct learner profiles: preservers, prudents, and pioneers. These profiles are characterized by varying levels of intrinsic technology barriers and technology acceptance. The findings reveal significant differences in deep and surface learning strategies among these profiles, with pioneers exhibiting higher technology adoption and deep learning engagement, while preservers show greater resistance to technology and a tendency toward surface learning. text_snippet: INTERPERSONAL TRUST AS A MEDIATOR BETWEEN INSTRUCTOR IMMEDIACY AND STUDENT MOTIVATION IN TURKISH HIGHER EDUCATION This study examined whether interpersonal trust mediates the relationship between instructor immediacy and student motivation in Turkish higher education, drawing on Social Exchange Theory. A quantitative correlational survey was administered to 564 undergraduate students from two public universities in Turkiye. Participants completed the Verbal Immediacy Scale, the Nonverbal Immediacy Scale, the Individualized Trust Scale, and the Student Motivation Scale. Exploratory factor analysis indicated a five-factor structure in which nonverbal immediacy bifurcated into positive and negative indicator subfactors; subsequent confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modeling tested a partial mediation model. The three immediacy dimensions significantly predicted motivation directly and indirectly through interpersonal trust, collectively accounting for 50.3% of the variance in motivation. title: GOVERNANCE BY DESIGN: AN AI–IOT READINESS AND EQUITY FRAMEWORK FOR LOW-RESOURCE SCHOOLS
text_snippet: GOVERNANCE BY DESIGN: AN AI–IOT READINESS AND EQUITY FRAMEWORK FOR LOW-RESOURCE SCHOOLS The rapid convergence of artificial intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) promises more intelligent, connected, and personalised learning environments, yet deployment in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) remains uneven and weakly governed. Much of the available evidence derives from campus-based and comparatively well-resourced educational settings, while existing studies often treat AI and IoT separately and give insufficient attention to equity, environmental sustainability, and institutional readiness. This study advances a Governance by Design perspective and proposes an AI–IoT Readiness and Governance Framework for low-resource schools and open and distance learning (ODL) systems, including open universities, dual-mode institutions, school-based distance programmes, and community or non-formal initiatives. It addresses three research questions: what enabling conditions are required for AI– IoT readiness in ODL; how AI–IoT-rich ODL environments can be governed to balance personalisation, security, and equity; and what transferable lessons can be generalised from early deployments in low-resource contexts. title: DISTANCE LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES AND SUPPORT SERVICES PROVIDED BY TURKISH UNIVERSITIES TO SUSTAIN EDUCATION
text_snippet: DISTANCE LEARNING TECHNOLOGIES AND SUPPORT SERVICES PROVIDED BY TURKISH UNIVERSITIES TO SUSTAIN EDUCATION Turkish higher education institutions (HEIs) have faced significant challenges in recent years (e.g., the COVID-19 pandemic and the Kahramanmaras earthquake on February 6, 2023) and were forced to transition to online platforms. Even before these challenges, support services for students and academics in distance education was deemed insufficient, a need further highlighted. Thus, comprehensive support in access, infrastructure, pedagogy, and psychological aspects is crucial. This study examined these gaps regarding the adoption of distance learning technologies and support services to sustain education in Turkish HEIs, particularly during times of crisis. We collected data from various online sources on a broad scale from 200 Turkish HEIs (fstate = 123, ffoundation = 77) out of 208. Inductive content analysis revealed that HEIs consistently adopted Learning Management Systems (f = 197) and virtual classroom platforms (f = 191). title: PEDAGOGICAL AND INSTITUTIONAL READINESS FOR TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION IN ONLINE EFL TEACHING: A QUALITATIVE STUDY AT TURKISH STATE UNIVERSITIES
text_snippet: PEDAGOGICAL AND INSTITUTIONAL READINESS FOR TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION IN ONLINE EFL TEACHING: A QUALITATIVE STUDY AT TURKISH STATE UNIVERSITIES The transformation of educational environments by digital technologies has made technology integration in online foreign language teaching a critical area of research. However, existing studies mostly focus on technical competence or attitude variables; research that addresses pedagogical and institutional readiness together remains limited. This study aims to examine the integration of technology in online foreign language teaching by EFL instructors within the framework of pedagogical and institutional readiness. The research was conducted using a qualitative case study design; data were collected from 42 instructors at state universities in Turkiye through open-ended forms and four focus group interviews and analyzed using thematic analysis. The findings indicate that technology integration is a multidimensional process shaped by the interaction of perceived competence, professional development needs, institutional infrastructure, support mechanisms, and psychological factors, rather than technical skills alone. title: A WEB-BASED INTEGRATED DIGITAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENT (IDLE) TO ENHANCE HIGHER-ORDER THINKING SKILLS
text_snippet: A WEB-BASED INTEGRATED DIGITAL LEARNING ENVIRONMENT (IDLE) TO ENHANCE HIGHER-ORDER THINKING SKILLS In the digital era, the development of Higher-Order Thinking Skills (HOTS) has become a crucial goal in science education. To address this need, the Integrated Digital Learning Environment (IDLE) was designed as an innovative web-based platform that integrates interactive student worksheets and a virtual laboratory for learning blood type concepts. This research was based on the 4-D model: define, design, develop, and disseminate. Expert validation studies demonstrated that IDLE fulfilled the “valid” requirements, with Aiken’s V ratings of 0.85 from content experts and 0.91 from media experts. Practicality assessment revealed that the platform received a “very practical” rating from teachers (87.78%) and students (81.10%). IDLE was evaluated for its effectiveness using a quasi-experimental study that included both an experimental group and a control group. The results of the independent samples t-test indicated no significant difference in pretest scores between the two groups, indicating equivalent initial HOTS levels. title: THE EFFECTS OF CHATBOTS-BASED INTERVENTIONS ON FOREIGN LANGUAGE SPEAKING PERFORMANCE: A META-ANALYSIS STUDY
text_snippet: THE EFFECTS OF CHATBOTS-BASED INTERVENTIONS ON FOREIGN LANGUAGE SPEAKING PERFORMANCE: A META-ANALYSIS STUDY The aim of this study is to examine the effect of chatbot-based interventions on foreign language speaking performance through a meta-analysis. Studies investigating the effects of chatbots on speaking performance were retrieved from various databases (e.g., ERIC, ScienceDirect, Taylor & Francis) using a range of keyword phrases. Following the inclusion and exclusion criteria, this meta-analysis included 16 experimental studies (k = 17) that implemented chatbot-based interventions to enhance learners’ foreign language speaking performance. All statistical data were collected and transferred to the Comprehensive Meta-Analysis (CMA) software to compute Hedges’ g values. The overall effect size of the intervention studies on foreign language speaking performance was 1.035, indicating a large effect. Intervention duration and education level were examined as moderator variables, but they did not significantly affect foreign language speaking performance. This study offers a theoretical basis for using artificial intelligence tools in language teaching by emphasizing chatbots’ potential to improve speaking.

title: THE EFFECT OF A FLIPPED CLASSROOM INTEGRATED WITH AN IMS BASED SIMULATOR IN MOODLE LMS ON STUDENTS’ ANALYTICAL ABILITY IN THE AUTOMATA COURSE
text_snippet: THE EFFECT OF A FLIPPED CLASSROOM INTEGRATED WITH AN IMS BASED SIMULATOR IN MOODLE LMS ON STUDENTS’ ANALYTICAL ABILITY IN THE AUTOMATA COURSE This study investigates the effect of a flipped classroom integrated with an IMS-based simulator within a Moodle LMS environment on students’ analytical ability in an undergraduate Automata Theory course. A quasi-experimental pretest–posttest non-equivalent control group design was employed, involving an experimental class that received simulation-based learning through a flipped classroom supported by Moodle LMS and an IMS-based simulator, and a control class that received conventional lecture-based instruction. Students’ analytical ability was measured using a validated assessment instrument, and statistical analyses were conducted to examine baseline equivalence and post-intervention differences between groups. The results indicated that both groups were equivalent at the pretest stage; however, the posttest results showed a statistically significant difference in favor of the experimental group, accompanied by a meaningful effect size. title: WHEN CHATGPT “FEELS LIKE FAMILY”: SERIAL MEDIATION PATHWAYS TO RELIANCE AND CRITICAL USE
text_snippet: WHEN CHATGPT “FEELS LIKE FAMILY”: SERIAL MEDIATION PATHWAYS TO RELIANCE AND CRITICAL USE This study aims to test the serial mediation pathway based on the expanded Affective–Behavioural–Cognitive (ABC) model to explain Reliance on ChatGPT (RC) and Critical Use of ChatGPT (CU) in an academic context. A cross-sectional quantitative survey study was conducted among multi-ethnic students in the coastal region of Southeast Sulawesi, Indonesia, in two stages: a pilot study (n = 72) to test the instruments and a main study (n = 287) to test the model. The analysis used confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) based on CB-SEM to validate the measurement model, and partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) to test the structural model through 5,000 bootstrap resamples (CI 95%). The results showed that the indirect serial effect from PCU to CU via EA/AIS-ST-RC was significant, whereas the direct path from ST to CU was not. These findings confirm that attachment to ChatGPT is not directly related to a decrease in CU. CU practices are primarily formed when User Stickiness (ST) has a positive and significant effect on RC, which is functional in completing academic tasks. Thus, RC acts as a proximal mediator in the relationship between ST and CU.

title: BRIDGING THE THEORY-PRACTICE GAP IN CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT WITH PEER INSTRUCTION IN JUST-IN-TIME TEACHING
text_snippet: BRIDGING THE THEORY-PRACTICE GAP IN CLASSROOM MANAGEMENT WITH PEER INSTRUCTION IN JUST-IN-TIME TEACHING Many think that universities can only teach inert knowledge. Flipped classrooms specifically, just-in-time teaching and peer instruction are two learner-centered strategies that have proven effective and popular, both when implemented separately and when integrated. This study proposes a PI-Based JiTT strategy enhanced by supporting technology. It tests its effectiveness in addressing inert knowledge in a pre-service teacher classroom management course from an attention control perspective. Two study groups participated in this study, one in a PI-Based JiTT class and the other in a conventional JiTT class. This study shows that the proposed strategy outperforms conventional JiTT classes in concept application and consistently improves pre-service teachers’ ability to apply concepts, regardless of attention control level. The implementation of the proposed strategy uses a digital training and assessment-based learning management system and a student response system, which help enhance interactive learning experiences, foster a culture of sharing, and encourage independent and cooperative learning. title: EQUALITY, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION IN OPEN AND DISTANCE EDUCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
text_snippet: EQUALITY, DIVERSITY, AND INCLUSION IN OPEN AND DISTANCE EDUCATION: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS Equity, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) have become central to educational discourse, particularly within the context of open and distance education (ODE), where digital environments demand inclusive and equitable approaches. Despite increased scholarly attention, research on EDI in ODE remains uneven, with limited interdisciplinary integration and geographic representation. This study addresses these gaps through a bibliometric mapping analysis of 1,013 publications indexed in Web of Science and Scopus between 2015 and 2025. Using the Biblioshiny interface of the Bibliometrix package in R, the study systematically identifies key contributors, influential publications, core research domains, and emerging trends in EDI research within ODE. Findings reveal a significant rise in EDI-related research since 2020, driven by the global shift to digital learning. title: DRAWING THE BIG PICTURE OF OPEN EDUCATION: A COMPARATIVE BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
text_snippet: DRAWING THE BIG PICTURE OF OPEN EDUCATION: A COMPARATIVE BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS This paper aims to provide a comprehensive overview of research on open education through bibliometric analysis. English-language articles published between 1955 and 2024 in the Scopus and Web of Science databases were selected for analysis. A variety of analytical techniques were employed, including descriptive analysis, co-authorship analysis, co-occurrence analysis, and citation analysis. The findings of this study indicated that research on open education steadily increased until 2020, after which it began to decline. The study also revealed that open education research is conducted globally, though it is predominantly concentrated in countries such as the United States and the United Kingdom. Furthermore, the majority of research in open education focuses on massive open online courses, followed by open educational resources. The International Review of Research in Open and Distributed Learning was identified as the journal with the highest number of open education articles across both databases. title: MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS’ EXPERIENCES OF ENGAGEMENT AND SELF-REGULATED LEARNING IN EDUCATIONAL INFORMATICS NETWORK (EIN)
text_snippet: MIDDLE SCHOOL STUDENTS’ EXPERIENCES OF ENGAGEMENT AND SELF-REGULATED LEARNING IN EDUCATIONAL INFORMATICS NETWORK (EIN) This study investigates middle school students’ engagement and self-regulated learning (SRL) experiences within the Educational Informatics Network (EIN). It specifically examines how using EIN influences changes in students’ SRL and engagement levels. The study employed an intervention design and involved 60 purposively selected middle school students. Data were collected using the MOOC Engagement Scale, the Perceived Self-Regulation Scale, and semi-structured student interviews. Quantitative data were analyzed using dependent t-tests, while qualitative data were analyzed through deductive analysis. The results indicated a significant increase in students’ SRL and engagement scores after the implementation. In particular, students developed several SRL strategies, including task management, time management, help-seeking, and self-evaluation. In addition, the findings indicated that students experienced behavioral, cognitive, affective, and social engagement, which were closely associated with their SRL development. Based on these findings, the study recommends improvements to the EIN platform to support students’ engagement and self-regulated learning better.

text_snippet: EXAMINING MARKETING STRATEGIES OF THE MAJOR OPEN AND DISTANCE HIGHER EDUCATION PROVIDERS This study was conducted to examine and compare the marketing strategies of open and distance education providers. In the first phase of this multi-case study, 10 universities from 10 different countries and 4 different regions of the world were selected for examination. Comparisons were also made between the West and the East, and between the public and private sectors. In the second phase, 10 institutions providing open and distance education services in Turkiye were selected for examination. Within this scope, 4 faculties and 6 distance education centers (DEC) were examined. This study was conducted to examine and compare the marketing strategies of open and distance education providers, investigate the differences between the strategies of public and private universities, and develop a series of marketing strategies for distance education services for higher education institutions. A qualitative multiple case study method was used to examine the marketing strategies of open and distance education providers. title: CLASSROOM DYNAMICS OF AI-SUPPORTED AUTOMATED WRITING EVALUATION IN AN EFL HYBRID FEEDBACK LOOP
text_snippet: CLASSROOM DYNAMICS OF AI-SUPPORTED AUTOMATED WRITING EVALUATION IN AN EFL HYBRID FEEDBACK LOOP This action research study examined how an AI-supported automated writing evaluation (AISAWE) tool can be integrated into EFL writing instruction through a hybrid AI+teacher feedback loop. Because classroom use of AISAWE can introduce feedback overload, interpretation problems, and concerns about learner agency, we implemented an eight-week exploratory action research (EAR) cycle to adapt instructional routines while documenting classroom uptake in a naturalistic setting. Data were primarily qualitative (field notes, teacher focus group data, and student reflections), supplemented by quantitative indicators (pre–post rubric scores, self-report scales, and the System Usability Scale) to contextualize patterns of change. Findings address three research questions. First, uptake was shaped by three recurring practices: managing feedback load, clarifying AI feedback through teacher mediation, and regulating reliance on AI feedback. Second, indicators showed gains in micro-level linguistic accuracy alongside stability in rhetorical structure across the cycle. title: NAVIGATING A PROMISING MEDIA OF DIGITAL COMIC FOR DISTANCE ENGLISH LEARNING: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
text_snippet: NAVIGATING A PROMISING MEDIA OF DIGITAL COMIC FOR DISTANCE ENGLISH LEARNING: A SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW Following the PRISMA framework, this research used a systematic literature observation method by analyzing 17 peer-reviewed articles from reputable indexed journals. The findings showed that digital comics effectively improve three key learning domains: reading comprehension, written production, and vocabulary acquisition. Moreover, this research revealed three prominent teaching methods integrated with digital comics: project-based learning, task-based learning, and autonomous learning. Furthermore, research results manifested popular platforms for creating and presenting digital comics: Pixton, Webtoon, and Toondo. A cross-country analysis highlights that research on digital comics is concentrated in Indonesia (76%), Ecuador, and Mexico, investigating how digital comics can address common challenges in EFL distance learning: low literacy rates, limited multimodal media, and bandwidth-friendly materials. title: DESIGNING AUGMENTED REALITY-BASED LANGUAGE LEARNING AND TEACHING MATERIALS WITHIN THE FLIPPED LEARNING MODEL: THE PERSPECTIVE OF IN-SERVICE EFL TEACHERS
text_snippet: DESIGNING AUGMENTED REALITY-BASED LANGUAGE LEARNING AND TEACHING MATERIALS WITHIN THE FLIPPED LEARNING MODEL: THE PERSPECTIVE OF IN-SERVICE EFL TEACHERS This mixed-methods study examines the views of in-service English teachers (INSETs) on augmented reality (AR) and flipped learning (FL). Twenty-three INSETs participated in a pre-test-post-test study, providing data via surveys and lesson plans. Six months later, a follow-up assessment evaluated how well teachers had integrated these strategies. The findings revealed a positive shift in perceptions of AR, highlighting its role in fostering collaboration, creativity, and efficiency. AR tools increased student motivation through interactive, multisensory experiences, deepening understanding and retention. Despite technical challenges such as cost and infrastructure constraints, teachers reported improvements in creativity, participation, and collaboration. AR helped transform traditional teaching into a more dynamic, student-centered approach. Teachers also favored FL, citing improved collaboration and access to materials outside the classroom. Benefits included improved student preparation, classroom interaction, and learner flexibility, whereas challenges included infrastructure, workload, and student motivation. title: MAPPING THE DIGITAL LITERACY OF INDONESIAN TEACHERS FOR PEDAGOGICAL READINESS
text_snippet: MAPPING THE DIGITAL LITERACY OF INDONESIAN TEACHERS FOR PEDAGOGICAL READINESS Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become a catalyst for educational transformation, underscoring the need to increase teachers’ digital literacy to utilize technology pedagogically. Although important, AI literacy as a teacher’s competence is still rarely studied empirically, especially in Indonesia. This study maps the level of AI literacy of Indonesian teachers and its relationship with pedagogical readiness, using a survey of 220 teachers from various regions. The instrument covers three dimensions, namely Digital technical competence, Ethical and critical awareness, and AI-based pedagogical practices. This dimensional structure is used consistently throughout the study. The descriptive analysis showed that the highest average score was in the AI in Pedagogical Practice dimension (Mean = 4.33), followed by Digital Competence (Mean = 4.29) and Ethical Awareness (Mean = 4.27). The correlation between Digital competence and Pedagogical practice was strong (r = 0.854). title: MOBILE MICRO-LEARNING ADOPTION AMONG ACCOUNTING STUDENTS
text_snippet: MOBILE MICRO-LEARNING ADOPTION AMONG ACCOUNTING STUDENTS The pursuit of professional accounting designations necessitates rigorous engagement with complex regulatory frameworks, often concurrently with full-time employment. While Mobile Micro-learning offers a solution through ubiquitous access to bite-sized content, it simultaneously introduces the risk of cognitive fragmentation. Moving beyond contextual replication, this study integrates the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology with the Value-based Adoption Model and Cognitive Load Theory. This theoretical synthesis allows for a rigorous evaluation of how extraneous cognitive load competes with perceived value in the high-stakes context of accounting education. Analyzing data from 342 Vietnamese accounting students via Structural Equation Modeling, the study identifies a critical tension between accessibility and concentration. The results demonstrate that while Ubiquity and Performance Expectancy are primary drivers of Perceived Value, Perceived Distraction and Information Risk serve as substantial barriers, significantly eroding the utility of mobile learning tools. This situation is no different from that of children in the archipelago in their attempts to strengthen their knowledge of Jawi script in both writing and reading. text_snippet: LEARNING ANALYTICS RESEARCH TRENDS IN TURKIYE: AN ANALYSIS OF POSTGRADUATE DISSERTATIONS Big data is essential for the sustainability and future of education. Learning analytics helps extract information from educational raw data, guiding data-driven decisions for learners and instructors. As studies on Learning Analytics continue to increase, examining research in a specific country provides valuable insights into the field’s development. In Turkiye, LA has been explored for over a decade, evolving in response to contemporary technological trends. This study analyses research trends in postgraduate dissertations on LA in Turkiye, using a systematic literature review to explore general trends, methodologies, and research outputs. The results indicate a massive preference for mixed research methods and educational data mining as primary research methods, while studies primarily involved university students as samples, using academic achievement tests and learning management system logs for data collection. Classification and parametric methods were implemented for data analysis, revealing that LA can effectively predict academic progress and identify success factors. title: EXPLAINABLE AI IN HIGHER EDUCATION ASSESSMENT: A BIBLIOMETRIC EXPLORATION OF AN EMERGING RESEARCH DOMAIN
text_snippet: EXPLAINABLE AI IN HIGHER EDUCATION ASSESSMENT: A BIBLIOMETRIC EXPLORATION OF AN EMERGING RESEARCH DOMAIN This study employs bibliometric analysis following GLOBAL recommendations to systematically map the emerging research landscape on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in higher education assessment, pursuing five objectives: quantifying research productivity, assessing geographic distribution, identifying collaborative networks, uncovering thematic evolution, and mapping intellectual foundations. We analyzed 72 peer-reviewed publications from Scopus spanning 2019-2025 to address a critical gap in systematic knowledge about AI transparency in educational contexts, particularly in response to regulatory frameworks such as the GDPR and the EU AI Act. The analysis reveals accelerating research activity, with publication output growing from single contributions in 2019-2020 to 26 documents in 2024 (R² = 0.7666). Geographic distribution shows China leading in productivity (8 documents) while Sweden demonstrates exceptional citation efficiency (25.50 citations per document), with European institutions collectively accounting for 35.4% of contributions. text_snippet: TPACK FRAMED DIALOGIC READING WITH DIGITAL VS PRINT STORYBOOKS: EVIDENCE FROM A PRESCHOOL INTERVENTION This study investigates the comparative effects of dialogic reading with digital and printed storybooks on preschool children’s early literacy development. Guided by the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework, the research examines whether digital formats, when combined with structured dialogic strategies, support literacy outcomes as effectively as print. A quasi-experimental pretest– posttest control group design was employed with 39 children aged 5–6 attending two public kindergartens in Istanbul. Participants were randomly assigned to an experimental group (n = 19), which engaged in dialogic reading via the digital reading platform, or a control group (n = 20), which used printed versions of the same texts. Both groups participated in eight small-group sessions (20-25 minutes each) over two weeks, facilitated by the researcher using scripted prompts based on PEER and CROWD dialogic reading frameworks. Data were collected using a researcher-developed Early Literacy Skills Evaluation Form measuring vocabulary acquisition, listening comprehension, and narrative retelling.
